items.question: What substance should be recognized as destroying wrinkles and gray hair?
premises: A specific nectar is indicated
It must be correctly recognized
It destroys wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: That nectar should be known as the destroyer of wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: One should know that to be the nectar which destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What bodily conditions are removed by the nectar's effect?
premises: Freedom from wrinkles and gray hair occurs
Freedom from all diseases occurs
Both states describe the same result
items.inference: The effect removes wrinkles, gray hair, and all diseases.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from wrinkles and gray hair and devoid of all diseases.

items.question: Where should the tongue be applied to destroy disease?
premises: The tongue is the instrument
The root of the palate is the location
The purpose is destruction of disease
items.inference: One should apply the tongue at the root of the palate to destroy disease.
items.plain_english: One should apply the tongue at the root of the palate for the destruction of disease.

items.question: How should the tongue be positioned regularly within the mouth?
premises: The tongue must be contracted
The practice should be constant
It should be joined within one's own mouth
items.inference: One should always contract the tongue and keep it joined within one's own mouth.
uncertainties: The exact anatomical sense of saṃyutam with sva vaktreṇa is context-dependent
items.plain_english: One should always contract the tongue, keeping it joined within one's own mouth.

items.question: What mental placement leads to the attainment of the unmanā state?
premises: The mind is placed in the heart
This placement is maintained
The practitioner reaches the unmanā state
items.inference: Placing the mind in the heart leads to attaining the unmanā state.
items.plain_english: Having placed the mind in the heart, one continues until reaching the state of unmanā.

items.question: What previously secret knowledge about time is now revealed to the goddess?
premises: The deception of time is the topic
It was well guarded
It has now been made manifest
items.inference: The well-guarded secret of deceiving time has been revealed.
items.plain_english: O goddess, the well-guarded deception of time has now been made manifest.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the section concerning the moon-island?
premises: The context is the moon-island
A chapter is being marked
It is identified as the sixth
items.inference: The sixth chapter concludes in the section on the moon-island.
uncertainties: The compound candra-dvīpa-vinirgate may refer to a specific textual section title
items.plain_english: In the section on the emergence from the moon-island, the sixth chapter concludes.

items.question: What teaching does the goddess request after declaring the lord her sole refuge?
premises: The goddess addresses the lord
She declares him her only refuge
She asks him to explain the three principles
items.inference: Having taken the lord as sole refuge, the goddess asks to be taught the three principles.
items.plain_english: Tell me of the three principles, O lord; I have gone to you alone as my refuge.

items.question: How should one contemplate what is present in the goddess's wheel?
premises: Something in the goddess's wheel is to be contemplated
The moon on the first lunar day is the analogy
The contemplation follows that likeness
items.inference: One should contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel as like the moon on the first lunar day.
items.plain_english: Contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel as the moon appears on the first lunar day.

items.question: Where is the flame-crest absorbed according to this teaching?
premises: The flame-crest is the subject
It is absorbed in that location
The location is the bone-wheel
items.inference: The flame-crest is absorbed there in the bone-wheel.
uncertainties: The exact referent of asthi-cakre is technical and context-dependent
items.plain_english: There indeed, O beautiful-faced one, the flame-crest is absorbed in the bone-wheel.

items.question: What qualities characterize the form that destroys wrinkles and gray hair?
premises: The form is fluid-containing
The form is black in appearance
It destroys wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: A fluid, black form is described as the destroyer of wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: It is a fluid, black form, and it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What kind of yogic practice should be applied at the support region?
premises: The location is the support region
Yoga is to be applied there
The practice is characterized as cool
items.inference: One should apply a cooling yoga at the support region.
uncertainties: The precise anatomical referent of ādhāra-skandha-saṃsthāne is technical
items.plain_english: One should apply a cooling yoga in the region of the support base.

items.question: How should the practitioner regard the sun and the moon in visualization?
premises: The sun is to be seen as an enemy
The moon is to be seen as a friend
Both are objects of deliberate visualization
items.inference: One should visualize the sun as an enemy and the moon as a friend.
items.plain_english: One should see the sun as an enemy and the moon indeed as a friend.

items.question: What kind of physical location is suitable for this practice?
premises: The place may be an earthen house or solitary spot
It must be free of people
It must be free of gnats and mosquitoes
items.inference: The practice should be done in a solitary, undisturbed place free of gnats and mosquitoes.
items.plain_english: In an earthen house or a solitary place, free from gnats and mosquitoes.

items.question: What additional qualities make a place auspicious for the practice?
premises: The place should be secluded and deserted
It should have a divine quality
It should be adorned with many flowers
items.inference: An auspicious place is secluded, deserted, divine, and adorned with flowers.
items.plain_english: In a secluded, deserted, divine place adorned with an abundance of flowers.

items.question: What level of attainment is realized after six months of practice?
premises: A period of six months is specified
Perfection becomes known after this period
The attainment equals the state of a yogini
items.inference: After six months, one attains perfection equal to the state of a yogini.
items.plain_english: After six months, perfection is known, equal to the state of a yogini.

items.question: What is situated at the brahma-knot as described to the goddess?
premises: The brahma-knot is the location
Something is situated there
Three are indicated as present
items.inference: At the brahma-knot, these three are indeed situated.
uncertainties: The referent of etāṃ and trīṇi depends on preceding context
items.plain_english: Situated at the brahma-knot, O beautiful-faced one, these are indeed the three.

items.question: What should be permeated by the fluid throughout the body?
premises: The fluid is the coloring agent
The entire body is the target
This includes the hair pores and so forth
items.inference: One should permeate the whole body, beginning with the hair pores, with the fluid.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one should color the whole body, beginning with the hair pores, with the fluid.

items.question: Within what timeframe is the promised result certain to occur?
premises: The result is affirmed to occur
There is no doubt about it
The timeframe is within six months
items.inference: The result certainly occurs within six months.
items.plain_english: It indeed comes to pass, without doubt, within six months.

items.question: What characteristics define the substance adorned with sixteen vowel sounds?
premises: The substance contains fluid
It is black in color
It is adorned with sixteen vowel sounds

items.plain_english: It is fluid, black in color, and adorned with the sixteen vowel sounds.

items.question: What rejuvenating transformation results from six months of dedicated practice?
premises: The practice is performed for six months
It is done repeatedly and devotedly
Even an old person becomes youthful
items.inference: Six months of devoted practice makes even an old person youthful.
uncertainties: The form taruṇā āyate is morphologically unusual and may reflect textual variation
items.plain_english: Through six months of devoted, repeated practice, even an old person becomes youthful.

items.question: What dark substance is accessed by resorting to the yogini's place?
premises: One resorts to the yogini's place
A substance is encountered there
It is dark and black-colored
items.inference: By resorting to the yogini's place, one accesses a dark, black-colored substance.
items.plain_english: Having resorted to the place of the yogini, one finds that which is dark and black in color.

items.question: How should the substance located at the hair, shoulders, and skull be applied?
premises: The substance is located at hair, shoulders, and skull

items.inference: One should color with the substance situated at the hair, shoulders, and skull by means of its splendor.
uncertainties: The compound keśa-skandha-kapāla-sthaṃ may refer to specific bodily locations
items.plain_english: One should color what is situated at the hair, shoulders, and skull by means of its splendor.

items.question: What ultimate freedoms are attained through this practice?
premises: Freedom from old age and death is attained
Freedom from disease and illness is attained
Both describe the final result
items.inference: The practitioner becomes freed from old age, death, disease, and illness.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from old age and death, and devoid of disease and illness.
